tools.name: Workflow
tools.description:
Execute a workflow script that orchestrates multiple subagents deterministically. Workflows run in the background — this tool returns immediately with a task ID, and a <task-notification> arrives when the workflow completes. Use /workflows to watch live progress.

ONLY call this tool when the user has explicitly opted into multi-agent orchestration. Workflows can spawn dozens of agents and consume a large amount of tokens; the user must request that scale, not have it inferred. Explicit opt-in means one of:
- The user included the keyword "ultracode" in their prompt (you'll see a system-reminder confirming it).
- Ultracode is on for the session (a system-reminder confirms it) — see **Ultracode** in the workflow authoring reference.
- The user directly asked you to run a workflow or use multi-agent orchestration in their own words ("use a workflow", "run a workflow", "fan out agents", "orchestrate this with subagents"). The ask must be in the user's words — a task that would merely benefit from a workflow does not count.
- The user invoked a skill or slash command whose instructions tell you to call Workflow.
- The user asked you to run a specific named or saved workflow.

For any other task — even one that would clearly benefit from parallelism — do NOT call this tool. Use the Agent tool (if available) for individual subagents, or briefly describe what a multi-agent workflow could do and how much it would roughly cost, and ask the user whether to run it. Mention they can ask for one with "use a workflow" in a future message to skip the ask.

Every script must begin with `export const meta = {...}`: a PURE LITERAL (no variables, calls or interpolation) giving the workflow's `name`, a one-line `description` (shown in the permission dialog) and optionally `phases` — one `{ title, detail? }` per phase() call, titles matched exactly. Pass the script inline via `script` — do not Write it to a file first, and do not also set the tool's `name` input (that selects a saved workflow); it is plain JavaScript, not TypeScript.

The canonical multi-stage pattern — pipeline by default, each dimension verifies as soon as its review completes:
  export const meta = {
    name: 'review-changes',
    description: 'Review changed files across dimensions, verify each finding',
    phases: [{ title: 'Review' }, { title: 'Verify' }],
  }
  const DIMENSIONS = [{key: 'bugs', prompt: '...'}, {key: 'perf', prompt: '...'}]
  const results = await pipeline(
    DIMENSIONS,
    d => agent(d.prompt, {label: `review:${d.key}`, phase: 'Review', schema: FINDINGS_SCHEMA}),
    review => parallel(review.findings.map(f => () =>
      agent(`Adversarially verify: ${f.title}`, {label: `verify:${f.file}`, phase: 'Verify', schema: VERDICT_SCHEMA})
        .then(v => ({...f, verdict: v}))
    ))
  )
  const confirmed = results.flat().filter(Boolean).filter(f => f.verdict?.isReal)
  return { confirmed }
  // Dimension 'bugs' findings verify while dimension 'perf' is still reviewing. No wasted wall-clock.

Before writing a script, load the `workflow-authoring` skill — the workflow authoring reference: script API and gotchas, resume, the **Ultracode** section, quality patterns, worked examples.

A workflow size guideline is configured for this session: medium — keep workflows under 10 agents. This is a guideline, not a hard limit — follow it unless the user's prompt calls for a different scale.

name.description: Name of a predefined workflow (built-in or from .claude/workflows/). Resolves to a self-contained script.

description.description: Ignored — set the workflow description in the script's `meta` block.

title.description: Ignored — set the workflow title in the script's `meta` block.

args.description: Optional input value exposed to the script as the global `args`, verbatim. Pass arrays/objects as actual JSON values, NOT as a JSON-encoded string — a stringified list breaks `args.filter`/`args.map` in the script. Use for parameterized named workflows (e.g. a research question).

resumeFromRunId.description: Run ID of a prior Workflow invocation to resume from. Completed agent() calls with unchanged (prompt, opts) return their cached results instantly; only edited or new calls re-run. Same-session only. Stop the prior run first (TaskStop) before resuming.

---
name: session-hygiene
description: "When a background session can be deleted, how Eric picks up where he left off, and the two scripts that do both"
metadata:
  node_type: memory
  type: feedback
  originSessionId: 25377000-859e-4d10-9d38-5e91339a12d3
  modified: 2026-11-04T23:44:38.395Z
---

Sessions are scratchpads; the repo (commits + `docs/STATUS.md` `## Next`) is the record.
Agreed 2026-10-02 after 79 sessions piled up on the home screen.

- **Delete a session** once its work is committed, pushed and in STATUS.md. Keep it while
  it is working/blocked, until its transcript (`~/.claude/projects/*/<id>*`) is committed
  and pushed in `~/.claude` (replaced the 24 h rule 2026-10-31; `claude rm` keeps the
  transcript file), or while its `jobs/<id>/tmp/` holds a git worktree.
- `python ~/.claude/scripts/session-sweep.py` prints KEEP / SAFE TO DELETE / repos with
  unsaved work. Read-only; `--delete` (added 2026-11-04) also runs `claude rm` on each SAFE id.
- **Start the day** with `python ~/.claude/scripts/where-was-i.py` (first `## Next` item
  per project, newest first; `--days N`, `--all`), then pick ONE thread.
- **Max 5 active threads** in global MEMORY.md; park one to add one. Parked NEXTs live in
  each STATUS.md.
- **One session per project**, named for the project; resume it or start fresh from
  STATUS.md instead of spawning a new session per small task.

**Why:** Eric works on many projects in a day and lost track of where each stopped.
**How to apply:** on "what was I doing" / "where did I leave off" run where-was-i; on
"clean up sessions" run `session-sweep.py --delete` (it calls `claude rm <id>` on each
SAFE id; claude rm refuses if the session's worktree has unpushed work). Never `rm` the
`~/.claude/jobs/` folders by hand. See [[post-merge-cleanup]].
/Users/kristinarash/DEV/DAILY.md:70:3. **When sessions pile up:** `python3 ~/.claude/scripts/session-sweep.py --delete` (lists, then runs `claude rm` on each SAFE one; drop `--delete` to only look).
/Users/kristinarash/DEV/DAILY.md:81:| Friday | `/weekly-review` (meetings, drift, the Friday sweep) |
/Users/kristinarash/DEV/WORKFLOW.md:184:| Friday | **`/weekly-review`**: syncs meetings, audits names, reports drift, digests the week's transcripts and action items, writes the review note, runs the **Friday sweep** (10 quiet paused projects: revive / keep 90 days / archive). |
/Users/kristinarash/DEV/WORKFLOW.md:201:| When sessions pile up | `python3 ~/.claude/scripts/session-sweep.py --delete` (deletes the SAFE ones; drop `--delete` to only look). |
/Users/kristinarash/DEV/WORKFLOW.md:217:| A project is drifting | Park it on the board, or let Friday's sweep decide |
/Users/kristinarash/.claude/scripts/session-sweep.py

content.text:
Base directory for this skill: /Users/kristinarash/.claude/skills/closeout

# Closeout

One command for the end-of-day sequence: day log → loose ends → memory → STATUS and handoff → commit and push → one verdict.

Step 0 asks Eric one question at most. After his answer (or when Step 0 is skipped), run every
other step without pausing: invoking closeout authorizes the whole sequence. Commit and push is
standing-authorized for every DEV repo (each repo's `AGENTS.md` Session routine ends with it, and
unpushed work on one machine is the top cause of conflicts on the other). On Windows or in Cowork,
read [`PLATFORMS.md`](PLATFORMS.md) for the commands that differ.

**Scope.** Every DEV repo with uncommitted or unpushed work (touched this session or not), plus
`~/.claude` (dotclaude), `~/.claude/skills` (claude-skills) and `~/.claude/global-memory`.
A repo whose `CLAUDE.md` says its data stays local (DexaProject is the precedent) is committed,
not pushed, and listed.

**Clear to sign off when** the closing `where-was-i.py --sweep` (step 4) shows no `ACTION` line
except repos listed under "Still open" with their reason, no background job is still writing,
`.errors.log` is empty or its entries are reported, and every repo touched today has a STATUS entry
dated today with a concrete first `## Next` item, and every `card-check` gap is fixed. Questions
only Eric can answer (a receiver nobody named, a decision recorded under `## Open questions`) do
not block: `/startup` shows them tomorrow; list them under "Still open" and say "Clear to sign off".
Anything short of that: "Not clear", naming the one thing blocking.

If a check fails and the fix is quick and safe (restage a file, clear a stale lock), fix it and
note it. A risky fix goes under "Still open".

## Step 0 — Day log (once a day)

Closeout is the one end-of-day step Eric keeps, so it carries the two inputs the biweekly
`status-report` trusts: the supervisor log and the shipped ledger. Before 2026-10-31 they lived
only in `interview-me` and `harvest`, and both lapsed (last log 09-14, last ledger row 10-06).

`{vault_status_log}` is `vault_status_log` in `~/.claude/skills/_shared/config.<platform>.json`.
When `{vault_status_log}/<today>.md` or `{vault_status_log}/.asked-<today>` exists, today's log is
already taken (usually by `interview-me`): leave out the three Part 0 questions and keep only
question 4, and only when step 1 finds a candidate. No candidate and no Front Burner question
(step 2 below) as well: skip this step.

0. **Front Burner checks** (plan `project-triage/docs/plans/2026-10-31-front-burner-self-maintaining.md`):
   run `python3 <dir of portfolio_json>/portfolio.py dates` and `... drift`. Resolve every line you
   can from evidence (STATUS dates, commits) with a cited `add-update` note. Every remaining line
   whose `needs_eric` is true (`--json`) becomes one more numbered question in step 2's batch:
   overdue step or no date → "done, new date, or no hard date?"; `off_board` → "start X?";
   `quiet` → "keep X or park it?". Ask every one, not just the first. Record answers the same day:
   one command per answer, `python3 <dir of portfolio_json>/portfolio.py decide X <action>`:
   done → `done --step N`; new date for an overdue step → `redate --step N --date YYYY-MM-DD`;
   a date for a row that has none (`no_date`) → `redate --date YYYY-MM-DD` (no `--step`: it adds one); no hard date →
   `no-date [--step N] --reason "..." --source "..."`; an old "no hard date" still true →
   `confirm-no-date`; a row with a dated step and an old record → `drop-no-date` (no question
   needed); keep a quiet row → `keep-quiet`; "no,
   leave it off the board" → `keep-off` (stores the exact moment, so only later work is asked
   about). Start or park with `set-status`. Do not hand-edit these fields. Skipped lines are not
   blocking: list them under "Still open".

1. **Ship candidates.** Read today's dated `## Current state` lines in every repo touched today
   (the sweep in Step 1 lists them; `landed.py show --days 1` also works). A candidate is work
   handed to a person or put in use: sent, delivered, shared, presented, merged for a user, live.
   Drop any project that already has a row dated today in the ledger (`{vault_output_ledger}`).
2. **Ask once**, all at once, short answers accepted: the three Part 0 questions from
   `interview-me/SKILL.md` (that file holds their wording; left out when today's log is taken), plus:
   > 4. Did anything ship or go to someone today? I found: <candidates, or "nothing">.

   then 5, 6, ... : one per Front Burner `needs_eric` line from step 0.
3. **Write the log** (only when you asked the Part 0 questions) exactly as `interview-me` Part 0 says (output format, honest-zero rule,
   append to an existing file). On an honest zero, write the empty marker
   `{vault_status_log}/.asked-<today>` instead, so the next closeout today skips the ask.
4. **Each confirmed ship:** run the `harvest` skill for it. Eric's yes is the ship evidence harvest
   Step 1 needs; the ledger row is the required part, lesson articles only when harvest finds them.

**Done when** the log file or the marker exists for today and every confirmed ship has a ledger
row dated today.

## Step 1 — Sweep

- **Repo sweep:** `python3 ~/.claude/scripts/where-was-i.py --sweep` (~4 s). It checks every git
  repo under `DEV/` (two levels) and the three config repos, and prints one line per repo needing
  attention; exit 1 means at least one `ACTION`. Another session, harness or machine may have left
  that work; name each such repo in the report. Flags:
  - `DIRTY`, `UNPUSHED`, `NO-UPSTREAM`, `BRANCH-AHEAD:<b>`, `BRANCH-UNPUSHED:<b>` (a local branch
    holding commits on no remote), `WORKTREE-DIRTY:<path>`: work not on GitHub. Step 4 pushes it.
  - `NOT-A-REPO`: a `.git` folder git cannot use, so the folder's work is tracked nowhere. List it;
    repair is project work, not closeout. It blocks only if this session wrote files there.
  - Info, never blocking: `STASH:<n>` (list it; leave the stash alone), `NO-REMOTE`, `DETACHED`
    (a pinned checkout), `LIVE` (session files the hooks rewrite every turn; the daily backup
    pushes them).
- **Background jobs** still running (shells, agents, workflows): wait for each to finish, or name
  it as the blocker. A job that writes after the push leaves work unpushed.
- **Registry drift:** `python3 <dir of portfolio_json>/portfolio.py crosswalk` (`portfolio_json` is
  in `~/.claude/skills/_shared/config.macos.json`). It only reports. List every item under "Still
  open", any folder created this session first (a project started without a row). Fixing waits
  for a project session. `drive_unreachable` means the Drive checks never ran: say so.
- Unfinished tasks from this session (TaskList), and anything promised to Eric this session and
  not delivered.

## Step 2 — Memory

Memory capture failing silently is Eric's top recurring worry; this step runs every time.

- **`~/.claude/global-memory/transcripts/.errors.log`:** surface every entry, fix the hook issue if
  obvious, then archive and clear it as in claude-stack-doctor's `FIXES.md` → Memory pipeline
  (append to `.errors-ledger.log`, then `cp /dev/null`). The file is tracked in `global-memory`,
  so this happens before step 4's push.
- **Today's transcript** `~/.claude/global-memory/transcripts/<today>.md` exists and changed within
  the last few hours.
- **New durable decision or active thread:** update `~/.claude/global-memory/MEMORY.md`
  (2,500-char cap; consolidate first) or write a Tier A memory with the `memory-write` skill.
- **Tier A stays on this machine** (its slug is built from the absolute path, which differs per
  machine). Every durable, project-scoped Tier A fact written today also goes into the repo:
  `docs/STATUS.md` for current state, `docs/DECISIONS.md` for a decision and its reason, the dated
  handoff for detail.

## Step 3 — STATUS, handoff, cards

**Handoff**, when real work happened (not just Q&A): `<repo>/docs/handoffs/<YYYY-MM-DD>-<slug>.md`;
workspace or system work with no single repo goes to `~/DEV/docs/handoffs/`
(`~/.claude/global-memory/handoffs/` is read-only history). Plain markdown that Codex,
Antigravity or a fresh Claude session can resume from:
- what was worked on and why
- decisions made, with the reasoning that would be lost
- exact paths of every file created or modified
- next actions, most important first
- anything mid-flight (open questions, awaited inputs)
- suggested skills: which ones the next session should invoke, by name

Link, don't copy: if a spec, plan, ADR, issue or commit already holds the detail, give its
path, URL or sha. Redact keys, passwords and personal data; the note is pushed to GitHub.

**`docs/STATUS.md`, in every repo touched, every time.** The next session reads it first, on
either machine, in any harness. Rewrite these sections in place, short:
- `## Current state`: two to five lines on where things stand today.
- `## Next`: most important first. Item 1 is one concrete action (a command to run or a file to
  open); `~/.claude/scripts/where-was-i.py` shows it to Eric the next morning.
- `## Open questions`: each decision waiting on Eric as its own top-level bullet, the question and
  enough context to answer it without opening another file. `/startup` lists this section across
  repos, so write the question itself, never a pointer. Mark answered items `ANSWERED <date>: …`
  or strike them (`~~…~~`). Leave the section empty when nothing waits.
- `## Gotchas`: anything that will bite the next session.

Over 20 KB, or more than 15 dated entries under `## Current state`: first move entries older than
14 days and finished `## Next` items, verbatim, to the end of
`docs/handoffs/STATUS-archive-<YYYY>-Q<n>.md`. The archive is a search root; entries move, they
are never deleted.

Then:
1. `python3 ~/.claude/scripts/where-was-i.py --decisions --days 1` prints what tomorrow's
   `/startup` shows as "Decisions waiting on you". Every decision left open today appears there as
   a readable question; fix the repo's `## Open questions` until it does.
2. `python3 <dir of portfolio_json>/landed.py scan --days 1` (~1 min), then
   `python3 <dir of portfolio_json>/portfolio.py card-check`. Fix every gap with
   [`CARDS.md`](CARDS.md), then re-run `card-check`.
3. `bash ~/.claude/scripts/harvest-dev-docs.sh`: copies every repo's `docs/*.md` into
   `~/.claude/global-memory/dev-docs/` (gitignored, indexed by memsearch). One line of output.
4. **Deliverables:** a finished file made for someone else today (PDF, deck, report, sheet) gets a
   copy in Drive `03_REPORTS`, uploaded through the API (writes through the `_DRIVE` mount hang):
   `cd <file's folder> && gws drive +upload ./<file> --parent 18lZZ4ep4pmK6upQfEcTUuLNlDdSAk5Au --name YYYY-MM-DD_<Sport>_<Topic>_<Type>_<Audience>.<ext>`.
   The repo keeps the source. Health data stays local.
5. **Front Burner phone page** (after Step 0's answers are recorded): render
   `python3 <dir of portfolio_json>/portfolio.py today --html <dir of portfolio_json>/outputs/front-burner.html`
   (allow-listed fields only: cleared names, fixed step labels, dates; it refuses an unsafe name).
   Then (1) `Artifact read` the `meta.artifact_url` in `portfolio.json` and confirm the header says
   **private**; if it is shared or unreadable, do not publish there: publish to a new artifact,
   put its URL in `meta.artifact_url`, and tell Eric once; (2) publish the file to that `url`;
   (3) `Artifact read` it again and confirm the header says **private** (owner only). If that read
   fails or shows it shared, the publish is not done: tell Eric at once that the page may be
   exposed, list it first under "Still open", and the verdict is "Not clear" until he has checked
   the page's Share menu. Needs a Claude session (Codex skips this step).
   A project row started today without `phone_ok` shows as "Project #n" until the `project`
   skill's name check clears it.

## Step 4 — Commit and push

- **Registry edits first, alone.** In project-triage, if `git status --porcelain portfolio.json`
  shows a change, commit that file alone as `data: board edits <YYYY-MM-DD>`. The board's "N
  unpushed registry edits" counts these; folded into another commit, they become a JSON merge
  conflict when the other machine edits too.
- **Before staging,** read the files about to be added (`git status --porcelain`). Anything the
  `BLOCKED` list in `~/.claude/hooks/session-autopush.js` names (`.env`, keys, credentials,
  secrets, token files, databases, DEXA) or over 50 MB stays out: add it to `.gitignore`, or leave
  it unstaged and list it. Health data never reaches GitHub.
- Every repo in scope: stage, commit with a descriptive message, `git pull --no-rebase`, push. On
  a merge conflict follow `dev-sync/SKILL.md` Step 3.3 (the one home for conflict steps), push, and
  list the file under "Still open". A side branch the sweep flagged: `git push -u origin <branch>`.
- `~/.claude/mods` changed this session: `bash ~/.claude/mods/mods-sync.sh`; list any invalid mod.
- **`global-memory` is pushed every time,** even on a light session: it is the only repo that
  carries memory to the other machine, and the nightly backup is too late for a same-day switch.
- Nothing to commit: one line, move on.
- **Prove it:** re-run `python3 ~/.claude/scripts/where-was-i.py --sweep`. Every `ACTION` line left
  is either fixed now or goes under "Still open" with its reason. A push that hangs is usually a
  credential prompt: look for `git credential-osxkeychain get` in `ps`; fix and retry once, as
  `~/.claude/projects/-Users-kristinarash-DEV/memory/project_brew-git-keychain-hang.md` says.
  Still hanging: "Not clear", that repo is the blocker.

## Step 5 — Verdict

`python3 <dir of portfolio_json>/landed.py show --days 1` lists every file that landed today (git in
every DEV repo, file times on Drive and in the vault), so the report names every created or
modified file with its full path. The ledger lives in `~/.claude/global-memory/landed/` and was
pushed in step 4.

```
## Closeout — <date>

**Day log:** written / honest zero / already taken today; **Shipped:** <ledger rows added, or "none">
**Committed & pushed:** <repos + one-line summary, or "nothing to commit">
**STATUS.md:** updated in <repos>
**Memory:** captured ✓ / issue found: <what> / skipped: <what> (Cowork)
**Handoff:** <path, or "not needed — no substantive work">
**Registry drift:** <N items, or "none">
**Still open:** <numbered list, or "none">

Clear to sign off. / Not clear: <the one thing blocking>.

**Landed:** <landed.py show output, grouped by project>
**Cards:** <card-check output after the step 3 fixes>
```

The block above the verdict line fits on one screen: Eric is leaving. Landed and Cards come last
because the next session picks up from them; trim both to projects with work today, keeping every
card that still has a gap.

Base directory for this skill: /Users/kristinarash/.claude/skills/closeout

# Closeout

One command for the end-of-day sequence: day log → loose ends → memory → STATUS and handoff → commit and push → one verdict.

Step 0 asks Eric one question at most. After his answer (or when Step 0 is skipped), run every
other step without pausing: invoking closeout authorizes the whole sequence. Commit and push is
standing-authorized for every DEV repo (each repo's `AGENTS.md` Session routine ends with it, and
unpushed work on one machine is the top cause of conflicts on the other). On Windows or in Cowork,
read [`PLATFORMS.md`](PLATFORMS.md) for the commands that differ.

**Scope.** Every DEV repo with uncommitted or unpushed work (touched this session or not), plus
`~/.claude` (dotclaude), `~/.claude/skills` (claude-skills) and `~/.claude/global-memory`.
A repo whose `CLAUDE.md` says its data stays local (DexaProject is the precedent) is committed,
not pushed, and listed.

**Clear to sign off when** the closing `where-was-i.py --sweep` (step 4) shows no `ACTION` line
except repos listed under "Still open" with their reason, no background job is still writing,
`.errors.log` is empty or its entries are reported, and every repo touched today has a STATUS entry
dated today with a concrete first `## Next` item, and every `card-check` gap is fixed. Questions
only Eric can answer (a receiver nobody named, a decision recorded under `## Open questions`) do
not block: `/startup` shows them tomorrow; list them under "Still open" and say "Clear to sign off".
Anything short of that: "Not clear", naming the one thing blocking.

If a check fails and the fix is quick and safe (restage a file, clear a stale lock), fix it and
note it. A risky fix goes under "Still open".

## Step 0 — Day log (once a day)

Closeout is the one end-of-day step Eric keeps, so it carries the two inputs the biweekly
`status-report` trusts: the supervisor log and the shipped ledger. Before 2026-10-31 they lived
only in `interview-me` and `harvest`, and both lapsed (last log 09-14, last ledger row 10-06).

`{vault_status_log}` is `vault_status_log` in `~/.claude/skills/_shared/config.<platform>.json`.
When `{vault_status_log}/<today>.md` or `{vault_status_log}/.asked-<today>` exists, today's log is
already taken (usually by `interview-me`): leave out the three Part 0 questions and keep only
question 4, and only when step 1 finds a candidate. No candidate and no Front Burner question
(step 2 below) as well: skip this step.

0. **Front Burner checks** (plan `project-triage/docs/plans/2026-10-31-front-burner-self-maintaining.md`):
   run `python3 <dir of portfolio_json>/portfolio.py dates` and `... drift`. Resolve every line you
   can from evidence (STATUS dates, commits) with a cited `add-update` note. Every remaining line
   whose `needs_eric` is true (`--json`) becomes one more numbered question in step 2's batch:
   overdue step or no date → "done, new date, or no hard date?"; `off_board` → "start X?";
   `quiet` → "keep X or park it?". Ask every one, not just the first. Record answers the same day:
   one command per answer, `python3 <dir of portfolio_json>/portfolio.py decide X <action>`:
   done → `done --step N`; new date for an overdue step → `redate --step N --date YYYY-MM-DD`;
   a date for a row that has none (`no_date`) → `redate --date YYYY-MM-DD` (no `--step`: it adds one); no hard date →
   `no-date [--step N] --reason "..." --source "..."`; an old "no hard date" still true →
   `confirm-no-date`; a row with a dated step and an old record → `drop-no-date` (no question
   needed); keep a quiet row → `keep-quiet`; "no,
   leave it off the board" → `keep-off` (stores the exact moment, so only later work is asked
   about). Start or park with `set-status`. Do not hand-edit these fields. Skipped lines are not
   blocking: list them under "Still open".

1. **Ship candidates.** Read today's dated `## Current state` lines in every repo touched today
   (the sweep in Step 1 lists them; `landed.py show --days 1` also works). A candidate is work
   handed to a person or put in use: sent, delivered, shared, presented, merged for a user, live.
   Drop any project that already has a row dated today in the ledger (`{vault_output_ledger}`).
2. **Ask once**, all at once, short answers accepted: the three Part 0 questions from
   `interview-me/SKILL.md` (that file holds their wording; left out when today's log is taken), plus:
   > 4. Did anything ship or go to someone today? I found: <candidates, or "nothing">.

   then 5, 6, ... : one per Front Burner `needs_eric` line from step 0.
3. **Write the log** (only when you asked the Part 0 questions) exactly as `interview-me` Part 0 says (output format, honest-zero rule,
   append to an existing file). On an honest zero, write the empty marker
   `{vault_status_log}/.asked-<today>` instead, so the next closeout today skips the ask.
4. **Each confirmed ship:** run the `harvest` skill for it. Eric's yes is the ship evidence harvest
   Step 1 needs; the ledger row is the required part, lesson articles only when harvest finds them.

**Done when** the log file or the marker exists for today and every confirmed ship has a ledger
row dated today.

## Step 1 — Sweep

- **Repo sweep:** `python3 ~/.claude/scripts/where-was-i.py --sweep` (~4 s). It checks every git
  repo under `DEV/` (two levels) and the three config repos, and prints one line per repo needing
  attention; exit 1 means at least one `ACTION`. Another session, harness or machine may have left
  that work; name each such repo in the report. Flags:
  - `DIRTY`, `UNPUSHED`, `NO-UPSTREAM`, `BRANCH-AHEAD:<b>`, `BRANCH-UNPUSHED:<b>` (a local branch
    holding commits on no remote), `WORKTREE-DIRTY:<path>`: work not on GitHub. Step 4 pushes it.
  - `NOT-A-REPO`: a `.git` folder git cannot use, so the folder's work is tracked nowhere. List it;
    repair is project work, not closeout. It blocks only if this session wrote files there.
  - Info, never blocking: `STASH:<n>` (list it; leave the stash alone), `NO-REMOTE`, `DETACHED`
    (a pinned checkout), `LIVE` (session files the hooks rewrite every turn; the daily backup
    pushes them).
- **Background jobs** still running (shells, agents, workflows): wait for each to finish, or name
  it as the blocker. A job that writes after the push leaves work unpushed.
- **Registry drift:** `python3 <dir of portfolio_json>/portfolio.py crosswalk` (`portfolio_json` is
  in `~/.claude/skills/_shared/config.macos.json`). It only reports. List every item under "Still
  open", any folder created this session first (a project started without a row). Fixing waits
  for a project session. `drive_unreachable` means the Drive checks never ran: say so.
- Unfinished tasks from this session (TaskList), and anything promised to Eric this session and
  not delivered.

## Step 2 — Memory

Memory capture failing silently is Eric's top recurring worry; this step runs every time.

- **`~/.claude/global-memory/transcripts/.errors.log`:** surface every entry, fix the hook issue if
  obvious, then archive and clear it as in claude-stack-doctor's `FIXES.md` → Memory pipeline
  (append to `.errors-ledger.log`, then `cp /dev/null`). The file is tracked in `global-memory`,
  so this happens before step 4's push.
- **Today's transcript** `~/.claude/global-memory/transcripts/<today>.md` exists and changed within
  the last few hours.
- **New durable decision or active thread:** update `~/.claude/global-memory/MEMORY.md`
  (2,500-char cap; consolidate first) or write a Tier A memory with the `memory-write` skill.
- **Tier A stays on this machine** (its slug is built from the absolute path, which differs per
  machine). Every durable, project-scoped Tier A fact written today also goes into the repo:
  `docs/STATUS.md` for current state, `docs/DECISIONS.md` for a decision and its reason, the dated
  handoff for detail.

## Step 3 — STATUS, handoff, cards

**Handoff**, when real work happened (not just Q&A): `<repo>/docs/handoffs/<YYYY-MM-DD>-<slug>.md`;
workspace or system work with no single repo goes to `~/DEV/docs/handoffs/`
(`~/.claude/global-memory/handoffs/` is read-only history). Plain markdown that Codex,
Antigravity or a fresh Claude session can resume from:
- what was worked on and why
- decisions made, with the reasoning that would be lost
- exact paths of every file created or modified
- next actions, most important first
- anything mid-flight (open questions, awaited inputs)
- suggested skills: which ones the next session should invoke, by name

Link, don't copy: if a spec, plan, ADR, issue or commit already holds the detail, give its
path, URL or sha. Redact keys, passwords and personal data; the note is pushed to GitHub.

**`docs/STATUS.md`, in every repo touched, every time.** The next session reads it first, on
either machine, in any harness. Rewrite these sections in place, short:
- `## Current state`: two to five lines on where things stand today.
- `## Next`: most important first. Item 1 is one concrete action (a command to run or a file to
  open); `~/.claude/scripts/where-was-i.py` shows it to Eric the next morning.
- `## Open questions`: each decision waiting on Eric as its own top-level bullet, the question and
  enough context to answer it without opening another file. `/startup` lists this section across
  repos, so write the question itself, never a pointer. Mark answered items `ANSWERED <date>: …`
  or strike them (`~~…~~`). Leave the section empty when nothing waits.
- `## Gotchas`: anything that will bite the next session.

Over 20 KB, or more than 15 dated entries under `## Current state`: first move entries older than
14 days and finished `## Next` items, verbatim, to the end of
`docs/handoffs/STATUS-archive-<YYYY>-Q<n>.md`. The archive is a search root; entries move, they
are never deleted.

Then:
1. `python3 ~/.claude/scripts/where-was-i.py --decisions --days 1` prints what tomorrow's
   `/startup` shows as "Decisions waiting on you". Every decision left open today appears there as
   a readable question; fix the repo's `## Open questions` until it does.
2. `python3 <dir of portfolio_json>/landed.py scan --days 1` (~1 min), then
   `python3 <dir of portfolio_json>/portfolio.py card-check`. Fix every gap with
   [`CARDS.md`](CARDS.md), then re-run `card-check`.
3. `bash ~/.claude/scripts/harvest-dev-docs.sh`: copies every repo's `docs/*.md` into
   `~/.claude/global-memory/dev-docs/` (gitignored, indexed by memsearch). One line of output.
4. **Deliverables:** a finished file made for someone else today (PDF, deck, report, sheet) gets a
   copy in Drive `03_REPORTS`, uploaded through the API (writes through the `_DRIVE` mount hang):
   `cd <file's folder> && gws drive +upload ./<file> --parent 18lZZ4ep4pmK6upQfEcTUuLNlDdSAk5Au --name YYYY-MM-DD_<Sport>_<Topic>_<Type>_<Audience>.<ext>`.
   The repo keeps the source. Health data stays local.
5. **Front Burner phone page** (after Step 0's answers are recorded): render
   `python3 <dir of portfolio_json>/portfolio.py today --html <dir of portfolio_json>/outputs/front-burner.html`
   (allow-listed fields only: cleared names, fixed step labels, dates; it refuses an unsafe name).
   Then (1) `Artifact read` the `meta.artifact_url` in `portfolio.json` and confirm the header says
   **private**; if it is shared or unreadable, do not publish there: publish to a new artifact,
   put its URL in `meta.artifact_url`, and tell Eric once; (2) publish the file to that `url`;
   (3) `Artifact read` it again and confirm the header says **private** (owner only). If that read
   fails or shows it shared, the publish is not done: tell Eric at once that the page may be
   exposed, list it first under "Still open", and the verdict is "Not clear" until he has checked
   the page's Share menu. Needs a Claude session (Codex skips this step).
   A project row started today without `phone_ok` shows as "Project #n" until the `project`
   skill's name check clears it.

## Step 4 — Commit and push

- **Registry edits first, alone.** In project-triage, if `git status --porcelain portfolio.json`
  shows a change, commit that file alone as `data: board edits <YYYY-MM-DD>`. The board's "N
  unpushed registry edits" counts these; folded into another commit, they become a JSON merge
  conflict when the other machine edits too.
- **Before staging,** read the files about to be added (`git status --porcelain`). Anything the
  `BLOCKED` list in `~/.claude/hooks/session-autopush.js` names (`.env`, keys, credentials,
  secrets, token files, databases, DEXA) or over 50 MB stays out: add it to `.gitignore`, or leave
  it unstaged and list it. Health data never reaches GitHub.
- Every repo in scope: stage, commit with a descriptive message, `git pull --no-rebase`, push. On
  a merge conflict follow `dev-sync/SKILL.md` Step 3.3 (the one home for conflict steps), push, and
  list the file under "Still open". A side branch the sweep flagged: `git push -u origin <branch>`.
- `~/.claude/mods` changed this session: `bash ~/.claude/mods/mods-sync.sh`; list any invalid mod.
- **`global-memory` is pushed every time,** even on a light session: it is the only repo that
  carries memory to the other machine, and the nightly backup is too late for a same-day switch.
- Nothing to commit: one line, move on.
- **Prove it:** re-run `python3 ~/.claude/scripts/where-was-i.py --sweep`. Every `ACTION` line left
  is either fixed now or goes under "Still open" with its reason. A push that hangs is usually a
  credential prompt: look for `git credential-osxkeychain get` in `ps`; fix and retry once, as
  `~/.claude/projects/-Users-kristinarash-DEV/memory/project_brew-git-keychain-hang.md` says.
  Still hanging: "Not clear", that repo is the blocker.

## Step 5 — Verdict

`python3 <dir of portfolio_json>/landed.py show --days 1` lists every file that landed today (git in
every DEV repo, file times on Drive and in the vault), so the report names every created or
modified file with its full path. The ledger lives in `~/.claude/global-memory/landed/` and was

```

**Day log:** written / honest zero / already taken today; **Shipped:** <ledger rows added, or "none">

Clear to sign off. / Not clear: <the one thing blocking>.

**Landed:** <landed.py show output, grouped by project>

# PFF Data Project — Agent Guide

This file is the canonical project memory for any AI coding agent working in this
repo. It is mirrored verbatim into `AGENTS.md` so OpenAI Codex (and any other
agent that reads `AGENTS.md`) gets the same context. A pre-commit hook in
`.githooks/pre-commit` blocks commits where the two files diverge.

If you edit one, edit both. See "Keeping CLAUDE.md and AGENTS.md in sync" below.

---

## What this project is

A standalone Python data pipeline that pulls Pro Football Focus (PFF) game and
player data into a local **DuckDB** database for Baylor University Football
analysis. Scope is **Baylor + every Big 12 team + non-conference opponents** for
the **current season plus two prior**.

The DB *is* the deliverable. There are no dashboards in this repo. Downstream
consumers — Power BI, Jupyter notebooks, and a future athlete management system
(AMS) project that will unify PFF with Catapult GPS, VALD ForceDecks, and Perch
VBT data — own visualization and cross-domain joins.

## Sister pipelines (do not modify from here)

- **VALD ForceDecks (CMJ/IMTP):** `..\..\ForcePlate_DecisionSystem` — the
  architectural template this project mirrors.
- **Catapult GPS:** `..\..\DataBase_GPS_Reporting`
- **Perch VBT:** not yet built.

The pattern across all of them is: per-domain Python pipeline → per-domain DB →
future AMS layer unions them on `(athlete_id, source_system, pulled_at)`.

## Tech stack

- Python 3.12+
- `duckdb`, `requests`, `python-dotenv`, `PyJWT`, `pyyaml`, `pandas`, `pytest`
- No web framework, no ORM, no dashboard libs — keep it lean

## Layout

```
PFF_Data_Project/
├── CLAUDE.md / AGENTS.md       # this file (mirrored)
├── README.md                   # user-facing setup and usage
├── requirements.txt
├── .env.example                # PFF_BASE_URL, PFF_API_KEY, BAYLOR_TEAM_ID
├── .gitignore
├── .githooks/pre-commit        # blocks CLAUDE.md / AGENTS.md divergence
├── run_pipeline.py             # CLI entry
├── config/
│   └── pipeline.yaml           # team/season scope, endpoints, retry config
├── src/
│   ├── db.py                   # DuckDB schema + connect + backup helpers
│   ├── ingest/
│   │   ├── pff_client.py       # PFF HTTP client (stub until Phase 0 done)
│   │   └── pipeline.py         # Orchestration: dims → facts → log
│   └── shape/transform.py      # JSON → tidy rows (teams/games/grades/stats/premium)
├── data/                       # small extracts only; the DuckDB lives at $PFF_DB
├── docs/
│   └── pff_api_notes.md        # Phase 0 spike output
├── scripts/
│   └── phase0_probe.py         # Credential discovery probe
└── tests/
    ├── test_db.py
    └── fixtures/
```

## Data model contract

Dimensions are stable identities; facts are timestamped measurements.

- **Dimensions:** `teams`, `players`, `player_seasons`, `games`
- **Facts:** `pff_grades` (per-player per-game, long form), `pff_stats` (extended
  stats, long form), `pff_premium` (advanced metrics, keyed JSON passthrough)
- **Operational:** `ingest_log`

`players` / `player_seasons` are derived from the grade rows (which carry
player_id, name, position, team_id, season) — cleanest "who actually played"
source; avoids the giant all-NCAA `/players` pull.

Every fact row carries `source_system = 'PFF'` and `pulled_at`. This is
non-negotiable — it is the contract the future AMS layer relies on to union PFF
with Catapult, VALD, and Perch facts.

`pff_player_id` is the durable join key. This pipeline does **not** maintain a
canonical athlete master record across systems. That mapping
(`roster.athlete_id → pff_player_id`) belongs to the future AMS project. Do not
invent it here.

## API contract (Phase 0 complete)

Full contract is in `docs/pff_api_notes.md`; OpenAPI specs in `docs/swagger/`.
Essentials:

- **Auth:** `POST /auth/login` with header `x-api-key: <key>` → `{"jwt"}`. Send
  `Authorization: Bearer <jwt>` on all calls. JWT lasts ~1h; re-auth on 401.
  Rate-limited (HTTP 429) — client backs off. `src/ingest/pff_client.py` owns this.
- **Base:** `https://api.profootballfocus.com`, league slug `ncaa`, season = year.
- **Baylor:** team_id / franchise_id = `118` (`BAYLOR_TEAM_ID` in `.env`).
- **Scope is open:** the key reads all NCAA teams + grades for any game, so
  Baylor + Big 12 + opponents is achievable despite the token's `franchise:118`
  constraint.
- **Play-by-play exists in the Video Feeds API** (EPA fields confirmed 2026-09-13):
  `/v1/video/ncaa/games/{game_id}/plays`, 330+ fields per play, including PFF EPA
  (`expected_points_added` and `expected_points_added_legacy`). Ingested for Baylor
  2024-2025 into `pff_premium` as category `video_plays` by
  `scripts/pull_video_plays.py`; deliberately not in `PREMIUM_CATEGORIES` (the
  season loop would pull every scoped game at ~1.5 MB each).
- **Full seasons stream from `/v1/video/ncaa/{season}/plays`** (~2.5 GB decoded,
  about a minute): `scripts/pull_season_video_plays.py --season YYYY` writes
  `data/video_plays_slim_<season>.parquet` (31 fields per play) and
  `data/video_games_<season>.parquet` (final scores; the plays feed only has the
  score before each snap). Both gitignored. `season_plays.to_frame` must build
  the frame with `dtype=object`: without it an int column with a gap becomes
  float64 and is stored as the text `"2.0"` and `"nan"`.
  Premium feeds (`/v1/premium/...`) provide play-level advanced metrics → captured
  in `pff_premium` as keyed JSON passthrough. All 12 API specs are in `docs/swagger/`.
- **FUTURE:** player-tracking feeds are deliberately not modeled in v1.

## Conventions

- **Credentials never in code.** `.env` only. Loaded via `python-dotenv`. The
  `.env` file is gitignored; `.env.example` is committed as the template.
- **DuckDB upserts:** use `INSERT OR REPLACE INTO` (idempotent refresh — re-pulling
  a week updates values rather than duplicating). See `_upsert` in `pipeline.py`.
- **Config path resolution:** always anchor to `Path(__file__).resolve().parent`
  walks, never relative paths from CWD. `run_pipeline.py` and `src/db.py` show
  the pattern.
- **The DB is not in the repo.** `src/db.py` resolves it from **`$PFF_DB`**, falling
  back to the old `data/pff.db` when the variable is unset. Windows:
  `%LOCALAPPDATA%\pff-data\pff.db` (set 2026-09-22). Mac: `~/.local/share/pff-data/pff.db` (set 2026-10-08 in `~/.zshrc`; the Windows laptop is hands-off). Reason: `~/Desktop/DEV` is a
  two-way Google Drive mirror, and Drive re-uploads and **locks** a 500 MB file on
  every write; on 2026-09-22 it held the file open against a running pull
  (`GoogleDriveFS.exe`). Keep the DB, its WAL and its backups out of the mirrored tree.
- **Backups before destructive ops:** copy the DB to
  `pff_before_<operation>_<YYYYMMDD_HHMMSS>.db` **beside it**, not into `data/`.
  `src/db.backup_db()` does this — use it from any new destructive code path.
- **Idempotent ingests:** running the same week twice must be a no-op.
- **One concern per module.** Client does HTTP. Shape does JSON-to-rows. Pipeline
  orchestrates. db.py owns the schema. Don't blur these.
- **Tests use mocked HTTP**, not live API calls. The Phase 0 probe is the only
  script that hits the real API.
- **No comments that narrate the obvious.** Comments are for non-obvious WHYs
  (e.g., "DuckDB requires ON CONFLICT here; SQLite syntax silently fails").

## CLI commands

```
python run_pipeline.py --dry-run               # auth + scope check, no writes
python run_pipeline.py --backfill              # full 3-season pull
python run_pipeline.py --season 2025           # full season
python run_pipeline.py --season 2025 --week 8  # one week
python run_pipeline.py --catch-up             # finished weeks still missing + latest week, then stats
bash scripts/weekly_pull.sh                    # the Wednesday 10:20 launchd job (ops/com.keystone.pffpull.plist):
                                               #   rolling backup, --catch-up, alert line in .errors.log on failure,
                                               #   DUE notices from config/checkpoints.txt
python run_pipeline.py --diagnose [NAME]       # query local DB
python run_pipeline.py --reset-db              # backup + reinit
```

Moving data between the Mac and Windows (never re-pull what the other machine already has):

```
python scripts/export_snapshot.py              # every season -> Parquet on Drive
python scripts/export_snapshot.py --season 2026
python scripts/load_snapshot.py --dry-run      # what would change here
python scripts/load_snapshot.py                # load what Drive has
```

## Moving data between machines

The DB never travels. `git` cannot hold a 600 MB binary and a live database inside a
synced folder gets locked and re-uploaded on every write. Instead each machine keeps its
own local DB and they exchange **immutable Parquet snapshots** through Google Drive:
written once, never mutated, so a half-synced file cannot corrupt anything.

- Root: `$PFF_SNAPSHOT_DIR`, else `.../00_Primary_Storage_Drive/pff-snapshots`.
- One file per table per season (`pff_grades/season=2026.parquet`), so a single season
  moves without dragging six million rows behind it. It is small: all of 2026,
  1.33 M rows, is about 6 MB.
- `manifest.json` records rows, bytes, which machine wrote it and when. An export
  merges into it, so exporting one season never erases the record of the others.
- The load merges by primary key and never deletes: snapshot rows are added or replace
  the matching local row; rows only this machine has are kept (the dry run says how
  many). Idempotent, and it backs the DB up first. It used to delete each season first,
  which erased the Mac's video_plays on 2026-09-22; `tests/test_snapshot.py` guards it.
- `ingest_log` is never exported. It says what **this** machine fetched; copying it
  would make the other machine's history a lie.
- After `dev-sync` pulls the scripts, run `load_snapshot.py` to pull the data. Git
  carries the code, Drive carries the rows.

## Testing

```
pytest tests/
```

Tests that need a DB use a per-test temp path; don't touch `data/pff.db`.

## Keeping CLAUDE.md and AGENTS.md in sync

`AGENTS.md` is a byte-identical copy of `CLAUDE.md`. The pre-commit hook at
`.githooks/pre-commit` blocks commits when they differ. Activate the hook once
per clone:

```
git config core.hooksPath .githooks
```

When updating agent guidance, edit `CLAUDE.md` first, then:

```
cp CLAUDE.md AGENTS.md
git add CLAUDE.md AGENTS.md
```

If you intentionally need them to diverge (tool-specific instructions for one
agent), update the hook before committing — don't bypass it silently with
`--no-verify`.

## Working with this repo from Codex

Codex reads `AGENTS.md` automatically. Everything above applies to Codex
sessions identically. Codex-specific notes, if any are ever needed, go in a
separate section here and get mirrored.


## Session routine
- Start: run `git pull`, then read docs/STATUS.md before doing anything else.
- End: update docs/STATUS.md (done, next, open questions), commit, and `git push`.
- Never leave uncommitted work at the end of a session.

A standalone Python data pipeline that pulls Pro Football Focus (PFF) game and
player data into a local **DuckDB** database for Baylor University Football
analysis. Scope is **Baylor + every Big 12 team + non-conference opponents** for
the **current season plus two prior**.

The DB *is* the deliverable. There are no dashboards in this repo. Downstream
consumers — Power BI, Jupyter notebooks, and a future athlete management system
(AMS) project that will unify PFF with Catapult GPS, VALD ForceDecks, and Perch
VBT data — own visualization and cross-domain joins.

## Sister pipelines (do not modify from here)

- **VALD ForceDecks (CMJ/IMTP):** `..\..\ForcePlate_DecisionSystem` — the
  architectural template this project mirrors.
- **Catapult GPS:** `..\..\DataBase_GPS_Reporting`

future AMS layer unions them on `(athlete_id, source_system, pulled_at)`.

- **Operational:** `ingest_log`

`players` / `player_seasons` are derived from the grade rows (which carry
player_id, name, position, team_id, season) — cleanest "who actually played"
source; avoids the giant all-NCAA `/players` pull.

non-negotiable — it is the contract the future AMS layer relies on to union PFF
with Catapult, VALD, and Perch facts.

canonical athlete master record across systems. That mapping

invent it here.
